industry.key: P. Energy, commodities and metals mining
industry.why: Neutral, from Overweight, on the row's own written condition ('to C if Brent is read under $85 or the industry's relative strength falls to C'): the relative strength leg fired. Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: C now, A prior at the industry (B at last week's reading), with Downstream distribution A and Upstream A against Services D, Agriculture D and Metals and mining F. The price leg moved the same way without firing: oil stayed below $100 as traders weighed Iran (Dow Jones Newswires, 5 November), against Brent near $115 at the 30-Oct-26 read, with hopes of a Middle East de-escalation (LBBW, 6 November). Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). The hedge this row was held for is being unwound in the price, and the industry letter was lending 30% of its weight to three sectors the market is selling. The view stays where the evidence is, in the sector rows: Downstream distribution Double Overweight, Upstream and Services Overweight, unchanged. No memo carried a congruence line this week. Counter-case: Iran supply risk is the one skew a source named for oil, and the two largest energy sectors still read A on relative strength, so this takes weight off the Pool's 18 upstream and downstream names a week before the tape might turn back. Back to B if the industry's relative strength returns to B with oil holding its level; the sector rows go to Neutral only if Brent is read under $85.

sector.why: Neutral, carried; the condition 'to D on a further F with the copper rally reversing' is half met. Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: F now, B prior, and F at last week's reading; but copper is at a fresh record on fears of a supply squeeze in one undated headline (MarketScreener) while another says commodities are on the back foot on subdued risk appetite and a firmer dollar (Newsquawk, undated), so the rally is not read as reversing. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). No Metals and mining stock is in the Pool. Counter-case for D: two readings at F is the market's view; for B: a record copper price. To D on a dated read that copper has reversed; to B if relative strength leaves F with a dated copper read.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the Bank of England's decision of 5-Nov-26 is still unread and the headlines disagree on it (on hold according to MarketScreener, cutting in 2026 according to the Irish Examiner, both undated); a weaker November consumer confidence headline (Trading Economics, undated) was not confirmed as a print for the window. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). 28 Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum; the book is 39% UK-listed by invested weight (component 5). Balanced on unread evidence, so Neutral is an absence here, not a judgement. To D on hawkish guidance when the decision is read; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.
